addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

FROM node:18-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      git \
      ca-certificates \
      curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Clone, pin to the base commit, then strip .git so the agent cannot inspect
# the fix PR or future history (anti-cheat). Re-init a single base commit +
# immutable tag so the verifier can reset test files; git apply still works
# without upstream history.
RUN git clone https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 0bcc55d2c8cdbf4decfc59e99f889694b52fcb52 \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Pre-install the repo's own dependencies so verify time does not wait on the
# network. npm ci honours the package-lock.json exactly.
RUN npm ci --prefer-offline 2>&1 || npm install

# Create workspace directories.
# tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image — the
# harness supplies them at verify time.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets

# Visual evidence, readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/.
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Behavioral verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-3020-mm
3	#
4	# Applies the synthetic test additions (Vitest + @vue/test-utils v1), runs the
5	# f2p/p2p tests that mount the real components against a stubbed game state and
6	# assert on what is rendered / clickable, then computes a reward from the JUnit
7	# XML report.
8	#
9	# NEVER greps source for the fix — it mounts the Vue components and checks
10	# the rendered output.
11	set -uo pipefail
12	
13	mkdir -p /logs/verifier
14	STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
15	STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
16	REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
17	
18	: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
19	: > "$STDERR_LOG"
20	
21	ensure_reward() {
22	  [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
23	}
24	trap ensure_reward EXIT
25	
26	cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
27	
28	# ── Step 1: Reset every path test.patch touches to its pristine harbor_base
29	# state before applying, so agent edits to tests cannot affect scoring and
30	# re-runs are idempotent. Use diff --git headers (present for text, binary,
31	# renames, and deletes) NOT +++ b/ (absent for binary/renames).
32	echo "== resetting test.patch paths ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
33	_patch_paths=$(
34	  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
35	    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
36	  } | sort -u
37	)
38	for _p in $_patch_paths; do
39	  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
40	    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null \
41	    || true
42	  # Scoped to the exact path (never its parent directory): a path like
43	  # vitest.config.js sits at the repo root, and `git clean -fd .` there would
44	  # delete every untracked file in the whole tree - including any new file
45	  # the fix itself adds outside src/__tests__/.
46	  git -C /app clean -fq -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
47	done
48	
49	# ── Step 2: Apply test.patch (adds vitest.config.js + src/__tests__/)
50	echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
51	git apply /tests/test.patch             2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
52	  || git apply --whitespace=nowarn /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
53	  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch     2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
54	  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
55	
56	# ── Step 3: Install pinned test-only dependencies
57	# @vitejs/plugin-vue2 needs vue 2.7.x and vue-template-compiler must match it
58	# exactly; the repo ships 2.6.x, so both are pinned here for the test run only.
59	echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
60	npm install --no-save --prefer-offline \
61	    "vitest@1.6.1" \
62	    "@vitejs/plugin-vue2@1.1.2" \
63	    "@vue/test-utils@1.3.6" \
64	    "jsdom@24.1.3" \
65	    "vue@2.7.16" \
66	    "vue-template-compiler@2.7.16" \
67	    2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
68	  || npm install --no-save \
69	    "vitest@1.6.1" \
70	    "@vitejs/plugin-vue2@1.1.2" \
71	    "@vue/test-utils@1.3.6" \
72	    "jsdom@24.1.3" \
73	    "vue@2.7.16" \
74	    "vue-template-compiler@2.7.16" \
75	    2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
76	  || { echo "ERROR: npm install failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
77	
78	# ── Step 4: Run the f2p/p2p tests, produce JUnit XML at $REPORT
79	echo "== running f2p/p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
80	npx vitest run \
81	    >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
82	  || echo "(vitest exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
83	
84	# ── Step 5: Compute reward from the JUnit XML
85	echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
86	# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
87	# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
88	# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-3020-mm
#
# Applies the synthetic test additions (Vitest + @vue/test-utils v1), runs the
# f2p/p2p tests that mount the real components against a stubbed game state and
# assert on what is rendered / clickable, then computes a reward from the JUnit
# XML report.
#
# NEVER greps source for the fix — it mounts the Vue components and checks
# the rendered output.
set -uo pipefail

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"
: > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() {
  [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
}
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 1: Reset every path test.patch touches to its pristine harbor_base
# state before applying, so agent edits to tests cannot affect scoring and
# re-runs are idempotent. Use diff --git headers (present for text, binary,
# renames, and deletes) NOT +++ b/ (absent for binary/renames).
echo "== resetting test.patch paths ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u
)
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null \
    || true
  # Scoped to the exact path (never its parent directory): a path like
  # vitest.config.js sits at the repo root, and `git clean -fd .` there would
  # delete every untracked file in the whole tree - including any new file
  # the fix itself adds outside src/__tests__/.
  git -C /app clean -fq -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# ── Step 2: Apply test.patch (adds vitest.config.js + src/__tests__/)
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply /tests/test.patch             2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply --whitespace=nowarn /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch     2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 3: Install pinned test-only dependencies
# @vitejs/plugin-vue2 needs vue 2.7.x and vue-template-compiler must match it
# exactly; the repo ships 2.6.x, so both are pinned here for the test run only.
echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npm install --no-save --prefer-offline \
    "vitest@1.6.1" \
    "@vitejs/plugin-vue2@1.1.2" \
    "@vue/test-utils@1.3.6" \
    "jsdom@24.1.3" \
    "vue@2.7.16" \
    "vue-template-compiler@2.7.16" \
    2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || npm install --no-save \
    "vitest@1.6.1" \
    "@vitejs/plugin-vue2@1.1.2" \
    "@vue/test-utils@1.3.6" \
    "jsdom@24.1.3" \
    "vue@2.7.16" \
    "vue-template-compiler@2.7.16" \
    2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: npm install failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ── Step 4: Run the f2p/p2p tests, produce JUnit XML at $REPORT
echo "== running f2p/p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
npx vitest run \
    >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(vitest exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# ── Step 5: Compute reward from the JUnit XML
echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-3020-mm.

Reads the JUnit XML report produced by vitest and computes a reward:
  1.0 — all f2p tests pass AND all p2p tests pass
  0.0 — anything else: a strict subset of f2p passing, a p2p regression,
        or the report is missing/unreadable

The policy is BINARY — there is no partial credit. A half-finished fix is
unsolved, so it scores 0.0; the per-test counts in reward.json carry how
close it got.

The report format is vitest's JUnit XML reporter:
  classname = test-file path  (e.g. src/__tests__/tickspeed-visibility.test.js)
  name      = describe > test name

IMPORTANT: this verifier NEVER checks source code for the fix — the reward
is derived entirely from test execution results.
"""

import atexit
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P = CONF["f2p"]   # list of f2p test identifiers (substring-matched)
P2P = CONF["p2p"]   # list of p2p test identifiers (substring-matched)
REPORT = "/logs/verifier/report.xml"

# --- canonical reward writer + --rubric gate ------------------------------------
# harbor parses reward.json as VerifierResult.rewards: dict[str, float | int] and
# takes it in PREFERENCE to reward.txt, so it must stay a FLAT map of numbers with
# exactly these seven keys. Registered with atexit so it writes last.
_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY — there is no partial credit.

    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still
    passes. A strict subset of f2p passing means the task is unsolved, so it is 0.0.

    reward is the same value, zeroed when the rubric judge failed a criterion. A
    "pass" or "not graded" verdict never lowers the score.
    """
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            json.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script
        # and the lighthouse UI read reward.txt. One dict means they cannot disagree.
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=sys.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail — including the empty string test.sh
    passes when no verdict was written — means "not graded", which must never
    penalise the run.
    """
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


def load_results():
    """Return {test_identifier: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from JUnit XML.

    Vitest's JUnit reporter puts:
      classname = the test-file path
      name      = "describe > it name"
    We construct the key as "{classname}::{name}".
    """
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        print(f"[verifier] WARNING: report not found at {REPORT}", file=sys.stderr)
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError as exc:
        print(f"[verifier] WARNING: XML parse error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return results

    for tc in tree.iter("testcase"):
        classname = tc.get("classname", "")
        name = tc.get("name", "")
        key = f"{classname}::{name}".strip("::")
        failed = any(c.tag in ("failure", "error") for c in tc)
        skipped = any(c.tag == "skipped" for c in tc)
        results[key] = "skip" if skipped else ("fail" if failed else "pass")

    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported test names.

    Accepts substring match or regex match so the config value stays
    short without fragile path duplication.
    """
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = None
        for k, v in results.items():
            if ident in k:
                hit = v
                break
        if hit is None:
            # Try regex as fallback
            try:
                pattern = re.compile(re.escape(ident))
                for k, v in results.items():
                    if pattern.search(k):
                        hit = v
                        break
            except re.error:
                pass
        out[ident] = hit or "missing"
    return out


def main():
    r = load_results()
    f2p_res = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p_res = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_pass = [k for k, v in f2p_res.items() if v == "pass"]
    p2p_pass = [k for k, v in p2p_res.items() if v == "pass"]

    reward = canon_reward(len(f2p_pass), len(F2P),
                          len(p2p_pass), len(P2P),
                          rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))

    print(json.dumps({
        "reward": reward,
        "f2p": f2p_res,
        "p2p": p2p_res,
        "f2p_pass_count": len(f2p_pass),
        "f2p_total": len(F2P),
        "p2p_pass_count": len(p2p_pass),
        "p2p_total": len(P2P),
    }))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
